_comment: The second-person sentences that face the paper rather than the subject.
Deliberately NOT the whole of the second person. The notes use "you" 74 times,
and most of it is ordinary English that would stiffen if it went: "similar to
how you are billed for gas or electricity" is inside a quoted definition,
"the drift rate is how you determine ..." is a statement about the subject, and
"how you find out why" is how the requirement is normally put. Removing that
would make the page more formal and less readable, which is the opposite of what
What goes is the second person that makes the sentence about the reader's
performance or about a question paper: "shows you know the distinction the
syllabus is drawing", "a question may ask you to place a service", "You manage
everything" where the other party is the customer and not the reader.
